title: Consumer Care Telephone Number Present
description: Detect whether a telephone number for consumer complaints is declared on the package. This check identifies the presence of a contact phone number. It does not verify that the number is active, belongs to the manufacturer, or is the correct contact for complaints.
amendment_status: Amendments 2012–2026 not text-verified. This rule is based solely on the original 2011 text.
applicable_scope: All pre-packaged commodities intended for retail sale, excluding: packages >25kg/25L (Rule 3(a)), industrial/institutional consumers (Rule 3(b)).

detection_method.description: OCR extracts all text. The system searches for phone number patterns (Indian format) in the label text, ideally near consumer-care-related keywords.

validation_logic.pass_criteria: A 10-digit phone number (with or without +91 prefix or 0 prefix) is found on the label.

evaluate.action: Filter out false positives using exclude_patterns (PIN codes, MRP values, batch numbers)
Check if any phone match is near consumer-care keywords (keyword_context)

If filtered_phones non-empty → DETECTED. If contextual_phones non-empty → DETECTED (high confidence). If phone matches found but all filtered out → UNCERTAIN. If no phone patterns found → NOT_DETECTED.

observable_evidence.description: What the software can observe: a 10-digit numeric pattern consistent with an Indian phone number (mobile: starts with 6-9, landline: starts with 0+area code), ideally near text like 'Consumer Care', 'Contact', 'Helpline', etc.
examples: Text 'Consumer Care: 1800-123-4567' detected — toll-free number found
Text 'PIN: 110001' detected but filtered (PIN code, not phone)

status_values.DETECTED: A phone number pattern was found on the label, optionally near consumer-care keywords.
status_values.NOT_DETECTED: No phone number pattern was found.
status_values.UNCERTAIN: A numeric pattern resembling a phone number was found but context is ambiguous (e.g., could be a batch number or PIN code).
status_values.NOT_APPLICABLE: Product is exempt under Rule 3 or Rule 26. Requires manual classification.

cannot_conclude: Whether the phone number is active or belongs to the manufacturer/packer
Whether the number is the correct contact for consumer complaints
Whether the number is a toll-free number, landline, or mobile
Whether the consumer care contact is a separate entity from the manufacturer
notes: Rule 6(2): 'Every package shall bear the name, address, telephone number, e mail address, if available, of the person who can be or the office which can be, contacted, in case of consumer complaints.'
The telephone number is mandatory. The email address is conditional ('if available').
This check focuses on the phone number only. Consumer care name/address is covered by MVP-A6.
Toll-free numbers (1800-xxx-xxxx) are common and should be accepted.
limitations: Based on original 2011 text only. Amendments may have added additional contact requirements.
OCR may misread digits (e.g., '0' as 'O', '1' as 'l', '5' as 'S').
PIN codes (6 digits) may be confused with phone numbers if not properly filtered.
Some packages print the phone number in very small font or on a non-principal panel.
The system cannot verify that the number belongs to the manufacturer vs. a third-party call center.
